payload.note: Contact-quotient's canonical computation uses the electroglottographic (EGG) signal: the contact phase is extracted from the EGG waveform via derivative zero crossings, and the quotient is the contact-phase duration divided by T0. The definition states the signal source is 'the electroglottographic or glottal-flow signal', but EGG is the primary modality — it is the direct measurement of vocal-fold contact that the parameter quantifies. Removing electroglottography as a capability would eliminate the direct measurement modality for this parameter; the parameter would lose its primary operational definition and relegate itself to an indirect glottal-flow approximation.

payload.name: glottal-flow-declination-rate
payload.scope: A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the steepest negative slope of the glottal airflow pulse within the glottal cycle (the maximum flow declination), built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter of the glottal source parameter set in speech science and laryngology.

definition.body: The glottal flow declination rate (GFD) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the steepest negative slope of the glottal airflow pulse within each glottal cycle: the maximum magnitude of the falling (negative) portion of the first derivative of the glottal flow, a measure of how abruptly the vocal folds close. Given the glottal flow waveform g(n) (the glottogram) and the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking, GFD is computed per pitch-synchronous cycle as max(-g'(n)) over the samples where g'(n) is negative (the first difference or finite difference of g within the cycle, clipped at zero), then aggregated across cycles by the median or mean over the analyzed voiced frames. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal flow waveform g(n) - the inverse-filtering estimate of the glottal source, the sole operand, (2) the fundamental period T0 from pitch tracking, which frames the per-cycle window, (3) the derivative operator - first difference or finite difference over the sampled flow, (4) the directional selection - the negative (declination) branch of the derivative only, (5) the cross-cycle aggregation (median or mean). A high GFD marks an abrupt glottal closure (pressed, spiky phonation); a low GFD marks a gradual, incomplete closure (breathy, hyperfunctional phonation), with maintained reference ranges separating typical from disordered phonation. It is reported in standardized units and persists as a member of the voice-quality measurement map: implemented in voice-analysis toolkits, documented in laryngology and speech-language pathology (the Dewaele glottal-source parameter set), and maintained alongside the maximum flow derivative, the glottal closure instant, the phase quotients, jitter, and shimmer. e.g.: GFD reported per frame in a laryngeal muscle-tension dysphonia study; GFD of a creaky-voice glottogram in a voice-disorder case report; GFD computed from an EGG-based glottogram in a pressed-phonation assessment | not: maximum flow derivative MFD (max magnitude of g' in both directions); return phase (a duration, not a slope) [formal: declivitas fluminis glottidis | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]

payload.name: apq1
payload.scope: To standardize the measurement of period instability in voiced speech for diagnosing voice disorders in clinical laryngology and speech science.

definition.body: APQ1 (average absolute difference) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the average absolute difference of the fundamental period between consecutive glottal cycles in a voiced speech signal. For N consecutive glottal cycles with periods P_i, the perturbation is computed as APQ1 = (1/(N-1)) * Σ_i |P_{i+1} - P_i| / ((1/N) * Σ_i P_i), reported in percent or in absolute units (milliseconds or seconds). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal segmented at pitch-synchronous cycle boundaries, (2) the per-cycle fundamental period measure. Small APQ1 indicates period stability (normal phonation); large APQ1 indicates period instability (dysphonia). Persistence mechanism: the standardized clinical voice-quality parameter computed by acoustic analysis software (Praat, laryngology toolkits) from pitch-synchronous period tracks; it persists as a documented measurement in voice-disorder assessment. e.g.: Praat's jitter analysis reporting the APQ1 value; the Kay Bolt Multi-Dimensional Voice Analysis software displaying APQ1 in its voice-quality report | not: jitter (the general category of period perturbation, not the specific APQ1 computation); shimmer (an amplitude perturbation parameter, not a period perturbation) [formal: titubatio quotiens media absoluta | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]

payload.name: apq3
payload.scope: To standardize the measurement of amplitude instability in voiced speech for diagnosing voice disorders in clinical laryngology and speech science.

definition.body: APQ3 (average absolute difference of amplitude) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the average absolute difference of the per-cycle amplitude between consecutive glottal cycles in a voiced speech signal. For N consecutive glottal cycles with amplitudes A_i, the perturbation is computed as APQ3 = (1/(3N)) * Σ_i |A_{i+1} - A_i| / ((1/N) * Σ_i A_i), reported in percent or in dB (20*log10(std/mean)). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal segmented at pitch-synchronous cycle boundaries, (2) the per-cycle amplitude measure (peak or RMS). Small APQ3 indicates amplitude stability (normal phonation); large APQ3 indicates amplitude instability (dysphonia). Persistence mechanism: the standardized clinical voice-quality parameter computed by acoustic analysis software (Praat, laryngology toolkits) from pitch-synchronous amplitude tracks; it persists as a documented measurement in voice-disorder assessment. e.g.: Praat's shimmer analysis reporting the APQ3 value; the Kay Bolt Multi-Dimensional Voice Analysis software displaying APQ3 in its voice-quality report | not: shimmer (the general category of amplitude perturbation, not the specific APQ3 computation); jitter (a period perturbation parameter, not an amplitude perturbation) [formal: scintillatio quotiens media absoluta | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes]
